33.name: Tic Tac Toe 3 in a Row
33.summary: Two teams race to shoot. A make earns the right to place a marker on a 3x3 grid. The first team to get three in a row wins.
33.easy: Reduce the distance to the hoop or use larger markers (like cones) to make the grid easier to see.
33.expert: Add a dribble move through cones before the shot to increase the challenge and pressure.
33.coachCues: Race for the treasure, Hero! Sink your shot to claim your spot on the grid and outsmart the opposition!

37.name: Escape Room
37.summary: Multiple Dribblers (Heroes) start inside the key with two Defenders (Guards). The Heroes must keep their dribble alive and avoid the Guards; once a specific signal is given, they must dribble out of the key to "escape."
37.easy: Start with fewer Defenders (Guards) or make the Escape Room (the key) larger to give the Heroes more room to move.
37.expert: Add more Guards to the room or require the Heroes to complete 5 crossovers before they are allowed to find the exit.
37.coachCues: Protect the Hoop Heroes Treasure! Keep your ball away from the Guards and use your Hero Agility to find the exit!

23.name: Team Battleship
23.summary: Cones are placed at various shooting spots to represent ships. Players work as a team to make a shot from each spot to 'sink' that ship. The goal is to sink theh entire fleet in the fastest time possible.
23.easy: Move the cones (ships) closer to the basket or allow the team to choose their favorite shooting spots.
23.expert: Add a 2-minute time limit or require a 'Swish' to sink the bigger battleships.
23.coachCues: Use your Hero Aim to sink the fleet! Communicate with your sidekicks to ensure every ship is targeted.

27.name: 21 Up Shooting
27.summary: Teams compete to reach 21 points first. Each player takes a long shot (2 points). If they catch the rebound before it hits the ground, they earn a bonus short shot (1 point). If the ball hits the floor, the turn ends.
27.easy: Allow the ball to bounce once for the bonus shot to help younger Heroes keep the game alive.
27.expert: Require the first shot to be from further out or start stronger team from a handicap  (eg -6) if playing multiple rounds
27.coachCues: Focus your Hero Vision! Track the ball early and use your speed superpower to snatch that bonus point before it hits the floor.

2.name: Money in the Bank
2.summary: Players in a line take turns shooting. Each make earns £1 plus whatever is currently in the bank. Misses add £1 to the bank for the next player. Most money at the end wins.
2.easy: Play Double Money rules where the bank total doubles after every miss so anyone can catch up quickly.
2.expert: Switch the shot type to layups or add multiple shooting spots around the court to increase the difficulty.
2.coachCues: Stay focused under pressure! Sink that shot to claim the cash!

6.name: 2 on 1
6.summary: Two offensive players attack one defender to find the best shot. Variation: 3 players pass toward half-court; the middle player drops the ball at the 3-point line and becomes defender.
6.easy: Start the offense closer to the hoop or limit the defender's movement to only the key.
6.expert: Add a 10-second shot clock to force quick decisions and rapid transitions.
6.coachCues: Find the open Player! Draw the defender in before unleashing the Super-Pass to your teammate.

78xivpmho.name: Rebound Relay
78xivpmho.summary: A competitive team relay drill where players battle to secure a rebound from a coach's intentional miss and score a putback to earn a point for their team.
78xivpmho.easy: Divide players into two teams at cones on the three-point line. The first player from each line starts under the basket. The coach shoots from the free-throw line, and the two players compete for the rebound and the score.
78xivpmho.expert: Introduce a 'no-dribble' rule where the player must score the putback immediately or after a single pivot. You can also have players start further back or add a second defender to increase the difficulty of the box-out.
78xivpmho.coachCues: Box out by positioning yourself between the opponent and the basket; keep hips bent, feet wide, and arms outstretched; secure the ball with two hands; pivot and lay it in.

52.name: Over / Under Passing
52.summary: Players are in pairs each player has a ball facing each other. They have to both pass to each other at the same time, one bounce pass under, one chest pass over. First Pair to reach target number (eg 20 passes, no drop) wins. Then reverse the rotation so each player has a turn at chest pass and bounce pass.
52.easy: Reduce the distance between the two lines or perform the drill while stationary.
52.expert: Increase the speed of the ball movement or add a dribble between passes.
52.coachCues: Rookies: Count to 3 then pass together! Rising Stars: Build a rythmn, add a dribble between each pass.

42.name: The Memory Game
42.summary: Two teams compete to find matching pairs from a set of giant playing cards. Players must make a shot before dribbling to the cards to turn over two. If a match is found they keep the cards; if not they turn them back over for the next teammate.
42.easy: Decrease shooting distance or allow players to turn over three cards to find a match.
42.expert: Increase shooting distance or require a specific hand for dribbling to and from the cards.
42.coachCues: Rookies: Use your Hero Memory to find the matching cards and power up your team! Rising Stars: Focus on a quick release and remember where the cards are hidden. Ballers: Snap your wrist on the follow-through and communicate with your team about the card locations.

46.name: Globetrotters
46.summary: Players perform a variety of ball-handling maneuvers including finger tips, around the head, around the waist, around both legs, and figure-eights through the legs. The drill focuses on developing hand-eye coordination, ball feel, and manual dexterity.
46.easy: Perform the movements while stationary or at a slow walk.
46.expert: Perform the movements while jogging or add a second ball for simultaneous handling.
46.coachCues: Rookies: Use your Magic Hands to wrap the ball around your body like a Hero! Rising Stars: Keep the ball moving fast and try not to let it touch your clothes. Ballers: Keep your head up, move the ball with your fingertips, and increase the speed of the wraps.

13.name: Pac-Man
13.summary: Players (Pac-Man) dribble along the court lines to avoid being tagged by designated "Ghosts." Everyone must stay on the lines; if tagged, you become a Ghost.
13.easy: Play without a ball first to master moving on the lines, or allow "Pac-Man" to jump between lines once per game.
13.expert: The "Ghosts" (taggers) must dribble a ball while chasing, or restrict everyone to using their non-dominant hand only.
13.coachCues: Power up, Hero! Stay on the tracks and use your Crossover Superpower to dodge the Ghosts!

17.name: Bull in the Ring
17.summary: Players form a circle with one "Bull" in the middle. Passers must keep the ball away from the Bull using fakes and quick passes. If the Bull touches the ball, the passer who threw it becomes the new Bull.
17.easy: Reduce the circle size or start with a slightly deflated ball to make catching easier; rotate the defender after 30 seconds if no touch is made.
17.expert: Add a second "Bull" (defender) to the ring or introduce a second ball to force rapid-fire passing and split-second decisions.
17.coachCues: Fake a pass to make a pass! Use your peripheral vision superpower to find the open Hero and keep the Bull guessing.

j46bvalwi.name: Jailbreak
j46bvalwi.summary: A high-energy game where dribblers start inside the paint and must escape past the three-point line within 8 seconds. Defenders line up along the perimeter and slide laterally to contain them. Players who successfully escape join the defensive line in the next round until only one 'jailbreaker' remains.
j46bvalwi.easy: Increase the time limit to 12 seconds or reduce the number of defenders to create larger gaps for the dribblers to navigate.
j46bvalwi.expert: Reduce the escape time to 5 seconds and require dribblers to use only their non-dominant hand to escape.
j46bvalwi.coachCues: Keep your eyes up to see gaps, protect the ball with your off-arm, and use change of speed to beat defenders.

i3qpszal0.name: Basketball Soccer (Two Ball Chaos)
i3qpszal0.summary: A dynamic, high-energy small-sided game that combines soccer and basketball elements to develop court awareness, scanning, and decision-making. Players use two balls of different sizes and point values simultaneously to score in baseline goals, forcing them to process multiple cues at once.
i3qpszal0.easy: Start with a single soccer ball on a full-sized basketball court to focus on basic movement, communication, and multi-sport coordination.
i3qpszal0.expert: Introduce 'Two Ball Chaos' by adding a second, smaller ball worth 2 points (versus 1 point for the soccer ball) and shrinking the court boundaries to force quicker decisions and more frequent transitions.
i3qpszal0.coachCues: Keep your head up to scan both balls; Communicate with teammates on which ball to pressure; React instantly to changes in ball possession; Evaluate risk vs. reward when choosing which ball to pursue.

47.name: Collect the Cards
47.summary: Players draw playing cards and perform a specific basketball task based on the suit: Hearts (Wall Passes), Spades (Shots), Clubs (Sideline Dribbling), or Diamonds (Waist Wraps). After completing the reps indicated by the card number, the player keeps the card. The goal is to collect the most cards within the time limit.
47.easy: Decrease the number of reps required for each suit or use a smaller area for dribbling.
47.expert: Add a second ball for dribbling tasks or require all shots to be made rather than just taken.
47.coachCues: Rookies: Draw a card to find your next Hero Mission! Use your Superpowers to collect the most treasure! Rising Stars: Focus on quick transitions between tasks and keep your energy high to win the race. Ballers: Execute each skill with game-speed intensity. Stay low on your dribbles and snap your passes.

comments.text: How does keeping the card work when there are 30 kids?

43.name: Stick or Twist
43.summary: Players progress through five shooting spots around the arc. On a miss, a player can Stick (stay at that spot for their next turn) or Twist (take an immediate second shot). If a Twist shot is made, they advance; if it is missed, they must restart the entire circuit from Spot 1.
43.easy: Allow two "Twist" attempts per spot or move shooting spots closer to the basket.
43.expert: Add a time limit to complete all spots or require a specific type of finish (e.g., swish only).
43.coachCues: Rookies: Do you feel lucky, Hero? Use your Superpower Focus to decide if you want to Stick or Twist! Rising Stars: Trust your form. If you miss, decide if you want to gamble to move forward or play it safe. Ballers: Check your stance and follow through. Make a strategic choice based on your shooting percentage from that spot.

16.name: Dribble Knockout
16.summary: All players dribble within a boundary. While keeping their own dribble alive, they must try to poke other players' balls out of the area. Last player standing wins.
16.easy: Start in a larger area like the full court to give more space, or allow players one "re-entry" if their ball is knocked out.
16.expert: Shrink the boundary to the key or the center circle to force tighter handle and more frequent contact.
16.coachCues: Protect the Hoop Heroes Treasure! Keep your body between the defender and the ball while looking for a chance to strike!

12.name: Chase Down Layup Drill
12.summary: One player (the runner) starts with the ball at half-court, while another player (the chaser) stands slightly behind them. On the whistle, the runner drives for a layup while the chaser tries to catch up and contest the shot cleanly.
12.easy: Give the runner a 2-step head start or allow them to use a 'Shield Dribble' to protect the ball.
12.expert: The Chaser starts sitting down or must touch a sideline before starting the pursuit.
12.coachCues: Ignite your Hero Boost! Finish strong at the rim before the defender uses their Hero Reach to block the shot.

26.name: Traffic Lights
26.summary: Players dribble their 'cars' across the court. On Green, they move fast; on Red, they must execute a perfect jump stop. If a player loses control or moves on Red, they return to the start. The first to cross the finish line wins.
26.easy: Start with just Red and Green lights, allowing players to use two hands to secure the ball during stops.
26.expert: Add a Yellow light for 'Retreat' dribbling  or a Blue light for 'Turbo' speed to challenge their gear shifts.
26.coachCues: Keep your Hero Vision on the coach! Use your low-dribble superpower to stay in control when the light turns Red.

22.name: Passing Hot Potato
22.summary: Players form a circle and pass the ball rapidly around. When the coach signals (whistle/stop music), the player holding the ball performs a fun forfeit (like 5 star jumps) before restarting. Focuses on quick release and hand-eye coordination.
22.easy: Start with players in a stationary circle and use a larger, softer ball to make catching easier.
22.expert: Add multiple balls to the circle or require players to use specific pass types (e.g., overhead or bounce pass) while moving.
22.coachCues: Hands ready, Heroes! Don't let the Hot Potato burn you! Quick chest passes to your sidekicks to keep the energy up!

0ytm9kg7u.name: Duck Tails
0ytm9kg7u.summary: A competitive tag-style game where players must maintain their dribble while attempting to pull 'tails' (scrimmage vests) from the waistbands of other players and protecting their own.
0ytm9kg7u.easy: Play in a larger area like a full half-court to provide more space and allow players who lose their tail to stay in the game and try to steal another one.
0ytm9kg7u.expert: Restrict players to using only their non-dominant hand for dribbling or reduce the playing area to the key to increase the speed and frequency of interactions.
0ytm9kg7u.coachCues: Keep your head up to see the floor, protect your tail with your body, and use quick changes of direction to escape dangerous situations.

7.name: Numbers Game
7.summary: Players are assigned numbers and sit on the baseline. When the coach calls a number, those players sprint to the ball in the middle to play 1v1 (or more) until a basket is made.
7.easy: For younger Heroes, use 2 balls so both players can score, or have the coach play as a "Hero Villain" defender against two players.
7.expert: Add more players as the round progresses to build from 1v1 to 2v2 and eventually 3v3 for a bigger challenge.
7.coachCues: Listen for your Number! Speed to the ball and  finish strong at the hoop.

3.name: The Weave
3.summary: Three players move up the court by passing and sprinting behind the person they just passed to. The drill ends with a layup and a return trip.
3.easy: Walk through the pattern first to master the follow your pass movement.
3.expert: Increase the speed to a full sprint and finish with a layup.
3.coachCues: Follow your pass to keep the weave moving fast.

36.name: Coach, What Time Is It?
36.summary: Players ask "Coach, what time is it?" The Coach calls out a time (e.g., "4 o'clock"), and players take that many dribbles forward. When the Coach says "Midnight!", everyone must dribble back to the start before being tagged.
36.easy: Shorten the distance to the Coach or allow players to keep one foot stationary while looking at the "clock."
36.expert: The Coach can yell "Lunchtime!" at any moment, requiring players to dribble to a specific "Cafeteria" cone before the Coach tags them.
36.coachCues: Listen for the chime, Hero! Keep your eyes on the Coach and use your Statue Superpower to freeze exactly on time!

32.name: Snake Races
32.summary: Two players race head-to-head through a zigzag cone course. The first player to successfully make their shot wins and stays in for the next challenger.
32.easy: Start with straight-line dribbling or fewer cones to focus on basic control and finishing at the hoop.
32.expert: Require specific advanced moves (e.g., behind-the-back) at each cone and finish with a reverse layup.
32.coachCues: Slither through the course, Hero! Use your Crossover Superpower to beat the rival Hero to the hoop!

tw03h3cd7.name: Keep Away
tw03h3cd7.summary: A 3v1 keep-away game played in a 10x10 foot square marked by cones. Three offensive players stand at different corners, leaving one corner free. They must pass the ball to each other without the defender intercepting it, moving to the open cone to maintain passing lanes.
tw03h3cd7.easy: Increase the square size to 15x15 feet to give the offensive players more space and time to react.
tw03h3cd7.expert: Add a second defender to make it a 3v2 drill, or restrict the offense to using only bounce passes.
tw03h3cd7.coachCues: Move quickly to the open cone, use pass fakes to move the defender, and target your teammate's chest when passing.

1.name: Freeze Tag
1.summary: Players dribble within a boundary while designated Taggers try to 'freeze' them by tagging them. If tagged stand with legs apart and ball in the air. If a team mate dribbles their ball through your legs you are unfrozen and rejoin the game!
1.easy: Reduce the playing area to to encourage more frequent stops and starts.
1.expert: The Tagger must also dribble a ball while trying to freeze the other players.
1.coachCues: Stay low like a Hero! Use your low dribble superpower to change directions.

28.name: Make for a cone game
28.summary: Two teams compete to score. For every basket made, that player takes a cone from the center pile and brings it to their team's base. The team with the most cones when the pile is gone wins.
28.easy: Move the shooting line closer to the basket or allow "Super-Sized" points (2 cones) for makes from a specific Hero Spot.
28.expert: Add a time limit or require players to dribble through a cone zigzag before they can take their shot for the treasure.
28.coachCues: Speed and accuracy, Hero! Sink your shot to claim the Hoop Heroes Treasure and build your team's base!

5.name: Team Tally Passing
5.summary: Two teams of 3 compete to make 5 consecutive passes without an interception then place the ball on the floor to score. No dribbling allowed. Interceptions only for defence.
5.easy: Add a Coach as a floating Super-Passer that both teams can use to keep the ball moving.
5.expert: Restrict the pass type to bounce passes only or increase the target to 10 consecutive passes to score.
5.coachCues: Protect the ball. Keep the ball moving with quick passes to outsmart the Defense.

gbftt3khv.name: Quick Draw
gbftt3khv.summary: A high-energy reaction drill where players dribble in place at the top of a triangle of cones. When the coach calls out a direction, players must quickly dribble to the corresponding cone and pull up for a jump shot. The first player to make the basket wins a point for their team.
gbftt3khv.easy: Perform the drill at a slower pace focusing on the stationary pound dribble and the shooting form rather than the race to finish first.
gbftt3khv.expert: Turn the drill into a high-intensity competition where players have a 1-minute time limit to score as many points as possible, emphasizing maximum speed and reaction time.
gbftt3khv.coachCues: Stay light on your toes, pound the ball using only your fingertips, explode toward the cone on the whistle, and maintain proper shooting form with eyes on the basket.

20.name: Snakes and Ladders
20.summary: Players dribble through a course of cones (the snakes) and an agility ladder (the ladders). They must perform specific crossovers and footwork patterns before finishing with a layup.
20.easy: Layups. Close up shots. Coach starts midway up ladder
20.expert: Harder shots, coach starts near top of ladder (no room for errors!) Or Coach jumps up 2 spaces if you miss, but only falls down 1 if you score!
20.coachCues: Players dribble through a course of cones and take a shot (layup/jumpshot) If they score the coach moves down the ladder, if they miss the coach climbs up the ladder. If coach gets to the bottom of ladder players win, if coach reaches the top they win!

9.name: Around The World Shooting
9.summary: Players shoot from seven designated spots around the key. After making a shot, the player moves to the next spot. The goal is to complete the circuit around the world as quickly as possible. Play in teams with a target number of makes to proceed to the next cone. Name the spots different countries!
9.easy: Move the shooting spots closer to the hoop or use a lower basket for younger Heroes.
9.expert: Add a time limit or require two consecutive makes at each spot before moving to the next level.
9.coachCues: Focus your vision on the rim! Step into your shot with your superpower stance for perfect balance.

24.name: Gates Passing
24.summary: Set up pairs of cones (gates) across the court. Players move in pairs, passing the ball to each other only when they are on opposite sides of a gate. The goal is to pass through as many different gates as possible in a set time.
24.easy: Place the gates closer together or use more gates to ensure every Hero finds a path.
24.expert: Add a 'Defender Shadow' who tries to block the gates, forcing players to use fake passes.
24.coachCues: Keep your Hero Eyes up! Find the open gate and snap a sharp pass to your sidekick.

30.name: Rebound Rampage
30.summary: Players compete for rebounds after a shot is taken. To earn the right to be a shooter, a rebounder must secure a set number of rebounds (e.g., 3). Shooters rotate out once a rebounder hits the target.
30.easy: Allow players to become shooters after just one rebound or move the shooting spot closer to the basket.
30.expert: Require players to secure three rebounds in a row before they can switch roles and become a shooter.
30.coachCues: Be a Rebound Hero! Use your strength to secure the treasure and your shooting superpower to bank the points!

34.name: The Floor is Lava
34.summary: Players must keep the ball moving through continuous passing without letting it touch the floor (the lava). The team works together to reach a target number of passes or move from one end of the court to the other.
34.easy: Play with "Safe Islands" (floor markers) that players can stand on to be safe from the lava while they look for a pass.
34.expert: Add a "Lava Monster" (defender) who tries to intercept the ball; if the ball touches the floor or a defender, the lava rises!
34.coachCues: Watch out for the lava, Heroes! Keep the Hoop Heroes Treasure in the air and use your Super-Pass to find an open teammate!

38.name: Basketball Tennis
38.summary: Two teams or players face off on a rectangular court divided by a center line. Players must bounce-pass the ball into the opponent's side so it cannot be caught after one bounce, scoring points like tennis.
38.easy: Start with a wider court or allow the ball to bounce twice to give Heroes more time to track the treasure.
38.expert: Shrink the court boundaries or require specific pass types like bounce passes only to increase the speed of the game.
38.coachCues: Ace it, Hero! Use your Hero Vision to track the ball and deliver a Super-Pass that stays within the lines!

10.name: End Zone Passing
10.summary: Divide the court into two halves with an 'End Zone' at each baseline. Teams must pass the ball up the court without dribbling. To score a point, a player must catch a pass while standing inside the opponent's End Zone.
10.easy: Allow offensive players one 'safety dribble' to escape pressure and keep the game moving.
10.expert: Add a second ball into the game or reduce the number of passes required to score to speed up the tempo.
10.coachCues: Protect the ball! Use your pivot superpower to find a gap and fire a laser pass to the End Zone.

49.name: Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Ball
49.summary: Players face each other with a ball on the ground between them. A coach calls out body parts (head, shoulders, knees) which players must touch. When the coach shouts Ball, players race to be the first to touch or grab the ball.
49.easy: Place the ball on a cone to make it easier to grab or slow down the pace of the calls.
49.expert: Add complex sequences (e.g., Left Hand-Right Knee) or require players to be in a defensive stance throughout.
49.coachCues: Rookies: Use your Superpower Reflexes! Listen closely to the Commander and grab that Hero Ball! Rising Stars: Stay on the balls of your feet and keep your hands moving fast. Stay focused on the prize.

14.name: Titanic
14.summary: Players take turns shooting free throws or spot shots. If a player misses, they move to the baseline (the "sinking ship"). They can be saved if the next shooter makes their shot. If all players end up on the Titanic it sinks and they have a forfeit (ie lap of the sports hall) But if last remaining player scores they save the whole team!!
14.easy: Give players two "lives" (misses) before they have to move to the baseline, or move the shooting spot closer to the hoop.
14.expert: Move players to more challenging spots around the arc or require a specific shooting routine (BEEF) before every shot.
14.coachCues: Don't let the ship sink, Hero! If you are the last player left score the gamewinner to keep the whole team afloat!

41.name: Diamond Passing
41.summary:
This is a youth basketball passing drill designed to improve players’ passing, footwork, pivots, and jump stops — all fundamental skills for the game. 

Setup:
        •        Use cones or markers to form a diamond shape on the court (a cone at each of the four corners).  
        •        Place an extra cone or object in the centre of the diamond.  
        •        Players line up at each cone or at designated starting points around the diamond.  

How it works:
        1.        The drill begins with one player holding the ball. That player dribbles toward the centre cone.  
        2.        As they reach the centre, they perform a jump stop (landing with both feet balanced) and come to a complete stop before making a pass.  
        3.        The player then makes a pass to the next player in the sequence (e.g., the next cone or line).  
        4.        After passing, the player follows their pass and joins the line where the receiver was standing.  
        5.        The receiving player then dribbles to the center and repeats the process — stopping, pivoting, and passing.  

Key teaching points:
        •        Emphasises ball movement and passing accuracy.  
        •        Encourages players to use both feet correctly with jump stops and pivots before passing.  
        •        Helps players learn to move into space and transition after they’ve passed the ball.
41.easy: Decrease the distance between cones and allow players to catch before pivoting.
41.expert: Increase passing speed and require a specific pivot foot (e.g., only reverse pivots).
41.coachCues: Rookies: Use your Owl Vision to find your teammate and snap the ball like a Hero! Rising Stars: Make a strong target and use a quick pivot to find the open lane. Ballers: Pivot on the catch, snap the ball with your thumbs down, and hit the receiver in the chest.

45.name: Rob the Nest
45.summary: Teams are stationed at corners with a center nest of balls. One player at a time sprints to the center, collects a ball, and dribbles it back to their hoop. Once the center is empty, players may steal from other nests. The team with the most balls at the end wins.
45.easy: Reduce the distance to the center nest or allow Rookies to carry the ball if they struggle to dribble while running.
45.expert: Require a jump stop and a ball wrap around the waist before placing the ball in the nest; allow stealing from other teams' nests.
45.coachCues: Rookies: You are a Speed Hero! Zoom to the center and use your Sticky Hands to grab the treasure! Rising Stars: Keep your eyes up while dribbling and protect your ball like a shield. Ballers: Stay low in your stance, explode to the center, and use a clean jump stop before every transition.

jfhegobu0.name: Sleeping Giant
jfhegobu0.summary: A high-energy, 'Red Light, Green Light' style game where players dribble towards 'treasure' (cones) while a 'Giant' (coach) has their back turned. When the Giant turns around, players must perform a jump stop and freeze; if caught moving, they must return to the baseline.
jfhegobu0.easy: Players dribble with their dominant hand and the Giant turns slowly, giving players more time to react and stop.
jfhegobu0.expert: Players must dribble with their non-dominant hand or two balls, and the Giant turns quickly and unpredictably to challenge their control and reaction time.
jfhegobu0.coachCues: Keep your eyes up to see the Giant, stay in a low stance, and 'stick' your jump stop to maintain balance.

18.name: Surprise 1v1 (Ball on Back)
18.summary: Offensive players start at the baseline and attack. On a whistle or signal, defenders (who were facing away or standing out of bounds) must sprint into the play to stop the score.
18.easy: Allow the offensive players to start with a live dribble to give them a bigger head start before the "Surprise" defense reacts.
18.expert: Add a second defender who must run around a further cone before joining the party to create a true recovery scramble.
18.coachCues: Shhh! It's a surprise! Wait for the signal, then use your Hero Speed to crash the party and protect the Hoop Heroes Treasure!

51.name: 1v1 Hand Off
51.summary: A player dribbles toward a teammate to execute a hand-off. Upon receiving the ball, the second player attacks the basket 1v1 against the original dribbler who has transitioned to defense. This drill focuses on timing, ball protection during exchanges, and scoring under pressure.
51.easy: Defender provides only shadow pressure; offense starts closer to the basket.
51.expert: Add a 10-second shot clock to force a rapid transition from the hand-off to the shot.
51.coachCues: Rising Stars: Use your body to shield the ball during the exchange and explode to the rim. Ballers: Attack the defender's top shoulder, execute a clean hand-off, and roll or space immediately.

nydlf0zyi.name: Hole in One Shooting Game
nydlf0zyi.summary: A competitive and fun shooting drill where players roll their basketball out into the court, sprint to retrieve it, and immediately take a shot from the spot where they picked it up. Players must choose a different starting position each round and compete to be the first to reach a designated point total.
nydlf0zyi.easy: Roll the ball a short distance within the key to ensure high-percentage shots and focus on basic shooting mechanics.
nydlf0zyi.expert: Incorporate specific shot requirements such as bank shots, floaters, or non-dominant hand finishes, and roll the ball further toward the perimeter.
nydlf0zyi.coachCues: Locate the rim early, square your feet quickly upon retrieval, and maintain a consistent follow-through under pressure.

50.name: Good Shot, Great Shot
50.summary: Three offensive players face two defenders. The player with the ball has a good shot but must decide whether to take it or pass to a teammate for a great shot based on the defensive rotation. The drill emphasizes unselfish play and high-percentage scoring.
50.easy: Start with stationary defenders who only provide light closing-out pressure.
50.expert: Add a third defender or implement a 3-second shot clock to force faster decisions.
50.coachCues: Rising Stars: Look for your teammate! A good shot for you might be a great shot for them. Ballers: Read the defender's feet. If they commit to you, find the open man. One more pass for the better look.

15.name: Caterpillar
15.summary: Players form a single-file line (the caterpillar), each with a ball. The last player in line must dribble to the front of the line while the others stay in place or jog slowly; once they reach the front, the new last player goes.
15.easy: Start with a shorter caterpillar (fewer players) or allow the front player to jog without dribbling to focus on the team movement.
15.expert: The caterpillar must weave through cones while moving, or the back player must perform a specific crossover before sprinting to the front.
15.coachCues: Stay connected, Heroes! Use your Caterpillar Superpower to move as one team while keeping your eyes up for the Hero Defense.

48.name: Find the Tennis Ball
48.summary: Teams compete to find a tennis ball hidden under one of twelve cones. A player must make a shot to earn the right to lift a cone. If the ball is found, the team earns points. The game continues until the ball is found or a target score is reached.
48.easy: Allow players to choose a cone after any made shot regardless of distance; use a larger target for shots.
48.expert: Require two consecutive made shots before a player can lift a cone; add a "penalty" object that subtracts points.
48.coachCues: Rookies: Use your Hero Sight to find the hidden treasure! Make your shot to unlock a cone! Rising Stars: Focus on your follow-through to earn a chance to hunt for the ball. Ballers: Stay composed under pressure. Communicate with your team to remember which cones have already been checked.

11.name: Basketball Rounders
11.summary: One team acts as 'runners' sprinting around the court perimeter (bases) while the other team acts as 'shooters.' Runners score points for every lap completed until the shooters make a designated number of shots to stop the round.
11.easy: Decrease the number of successful shots required by the shooters to stop the runners.
11.expert: Add a second runner to the base path or increase the distance of the shooting spots.
11.coachCues: Sprinting speed is your superpower! Shooters, use your Hero Focus to sink those baskets and stop the clock.

19.name: The Gauntlet
19.summary: Dribblers must navigate through three distinct lanes or lines of defenders. Each line of defense is progressively more difficult. The goal is to reach the end and score without losing the ball.
19.easy: Start with fewer defenders or give the offensive player a "Superpower Shield" (one free restart if they lose the ball).
19.expert: Add more defenders to the Gauntlet or require the dribbler to finish with a specific move, like a reverse layup, at the end.
19.coachCues: Navigate the Gauntlet, Hero! Use your Crossover Superpower to slip past the Hero Defense and reach the treasure!

44.name: Gimme 5 Dribbling
44.summary: Players dribble around the a half court space giving other players a "high five with their non dribbling hand. Play short rounds of 30 seconds to see how many high fives players can complete.
44.coachCues: Rookies: Keep your head up to see the other players in good time.

40.name: Train Start
40.summary: Players stand in a line, facing the same direction. The player at the front has a ball (offense) then alternate defence/offence/defence and so on starting inside the paint under the hoop the 'Train' should have 4 or 6 players (so it becomes 2v2 or 3v3). The player at the front dribbles the ball out into any space and the other players all sprint to space then the game begins 2v2 or 3v3. The 'Train' is basically a different way to start the small sided game and encourage players to find space.
40.easy: Have players stand closer together so the "engine" signal travels faster through the train.
40.expert: Require players to dribble with their non-dominant hand or perform a crossover when they reach the front of the train.
40.coachCues: Full steam ahead, Heroes! Use your Hero Hearing to catch the signal and keep the Hoop Heroes Train moving!

35.name: Sharks and Minnows
35.summary: Minnows dribble from one baseline to the other while designated Sharks in the middle try to tag them or poke the ball away. If a Minnow is tagged or loses their ball, they become a Shark for the next round.
35.easy: Start with a wider boundary or have the Shark hop on one leg to give the Minnows a better chance to escape.
35.expert: The Sharks must also dribble a ball while hunting, or require Minnows to use only their non-dominant hand to cross the ocean.
35.coachCues: Watch out for the Hero Sharks! Keep your eyes up and use your Crossover Superpower to protect the treasure and reach the safe shore!

31.name: On the Board
31.summary: Offense and defense line up. The coach shoots or throws the ball against the backboard. Both players must fight for position and compete to grab the rebound.
31.easy: Allow the offense to start closer to the basket or give them a "free" jump before the defender can move.
31.expert: Add a second offensive player to make it 2 on 1, forcing the defender to box out one while tracking the other.
31.coachCues: Find your player and seal them! Use your Hero Strength to own the paint and grab that Hoop Heroes Treasure off the glass!

39.name: Free Throw Golf
39.summary: Playing as a team of 3-4, Players shoot free throws in rounds. A made shot is -1 point (birdie), a miss is +1 point (bogey). The team with the lowest score after 18 "holes" (shots) wins.
39.easy: Decrease the winning score to 9 or let players start closer to the hoop to build confidence.
39.expert: Require a "swish" to count as -1 point; if the ball hits the rim and goes in, it counts as 0 (par).
39.coachCues: Keep your cool, Hero! Use your Laser-Focus superpower to sink the shot and get the lowest score on the course!

29.name: Switch Up
29.summary: Players work in groups of 3 in a rectangle, one player each end and one in the middle (marked by cones). Player in middle passes ball to player at one end who then tried to dribble past them, once they get past they become the middle player and pass to the other player at the end who then tried to dribble past, so players 'switch up' every time with middle player as the passer and defender.
29.easy: Start the drill at half speed to help players recognize the change in roles.
29.expert: Add a second ball to the court to force players to track multiple threats during the transition.
29.coachCues: Quick switch, Hero! Use your Hero Awareness to snap from offense to defense in a flash!

4.name: Rock, Paper, Scissors, SHOOT!
4.summary: Players dribble around the court; meeting a peer triggers a Rock, Paper, Scissors game with the ball between feet. Winners shoot; losers perform a quick exercise.
4.easy: Reduce the area to just the half-court or key to ensure players meet more frequently.
4.expert: Require winners to perform a specific dribble move (e.g., between-the-legs) before their shot.
4.coachCues: Eyes up! Dribble through the crowd, find a partner, and show your Rock, Paper, Scissors superpower!

8.name: Bulldozers and Builders / Construction Site
8.summary: Scatter cones across the court, half standing up and half knocked over. Divide players into two teams: Bulldozers (who try to knock standing cones over) and Builders (who try to stand them up). Players must move through the 'Construction Site' and finish with the most cones in their team's position.
8.easy: Start with fewer cones and allow Builders to use their hands to fix the cones while stationary.
8.expert: Add more cones and require all players (Bulldozers and Builders) to dribble a basketball throughout the entire game.
8.coachCues: Protect the site! Use your Dribble to keep the ball safe while you flip the cones.

25.name: The Deny Layup Drill
25.summary: A defender works to deny an offensive player from receiving a pass on the wing. If the offensive player manages to catch the ball, they immediately drive for a layup while the defender recovers to contest the shot.
25.easy: The defender starts with one hand on the offensive player’s shoulder to stay connected and practice the feel of the Hero Shadow.
25.expert: Add a second offensive player at the opposite wing to force the defender to track multiple Hero Targets.
25.coachCues: Activate your Hero Shadow! Stay between your player and the ball, using your Hero Reach to deny the pass.

21.name: Shield Tag
21.summary: Players dribble within a designated area while one or more taggers try to touch their ball. Dribblers must use their off-arm to shield the ball and maintain control while moving away from pressure.
21.easy: Reduce the boundary size to increase frequency of player interaction and forced stops.
21.expert: Require players to use their non-dominant hand only or add a second tagger to increase defensive pressure.
21.coachCues: Protect the Hoop Heroes Treasure! Use your arm as a shield and keep your body between the defender and the ball.
